Bug_Title: Classes should not access their own subclasses during class initialization
Bug_Explanation: In the noncompliant code, Parent class is referencing a static method of its subclass, Child, during its own initialization, which is a violation of this rule. The execution of the program will highly rely on the order of the class initialization and static members. This could lead to an 'initialization cycle' or even a deadlock in some corner cases. Moreover, if the order of the static class members is changed, the behavior of the program might change. These issues can be very hard to diagnose so it is highly recommended to avoid creating this kind of dependencies.
